_note: Plain-English meanings for registry (whois) keys and inetnum/inet6num status values. Status keys are upper-case with '-' and '_' turned into spaces.

keys.inetnum: The IPv4 address range this record describes.
keys.inet6num: The IPv6 address range this record describes.
keys.netrange: The IPv4 address range this record describes.
keys.cidr: The same address range written as a prefix.
keys.netname: A short machine-friendly name the registry holder gave this block.
keys.nettype: How the registry classifies this block (direct allocation, reassignment and so on).
keys.descr: Free-text description, usually the organisation using the block.
keys.orgname: Name of the organisation that holds the block.
keys.org-name: Name of the organisation that holds the block.
keys.organization: Name of the organisation that holds the block.
keys.owner: Name of the organisation that holds the block.
keys.org: Handle of the organisation object that holds the block.
keys.country: Country the holder registered for this block. It is not proof of where the servers are.
keys.admin-c: Administrative contact handle: who is responsible for the block.
keys.tech-c: Technical contact handle: who to ask about the network.
keys.abuse-c: Abuse contact handle: where to report spam or attacks from this block.
keys.abuse-mailbox: Mailbox that receives abuse reports for this block.
keys.mnt-by: Maintainer that is allowed to change this record.
keys.mnt-lower: Maintainer that may create more-specific records inside this block.
keys.mnt-routes: Maintainer that may create route objects for this block.
keys.mnt-domains: Maintainer that may create reverse-DNS domain objects for this block.
keys.mnt-irt: Incident-response team contact for this block.
keys.irt: Incident-response team object linked to this block.
keys.status: How the registry classifies this block. See the status table for what each value means.
keys.created: Date the record was first created.
keys.last-modified: When the record was last changed.
keys.updated: When the record was last changed.
keys.source: Which registry database this record came from.
keys.geofeed: URL of a geolocation feed (RFC 8805) where the holder publishes where each prefix is used.
keys.parent: The larger block this record sits inside.
keys.organization-id: Registry handle of the holder organisation.
keys.originas: AS number the holder says will announce the block.
keys.route: The prefix this route object covers.
keys.route6: The IPv6 prefix this route object covers.
keys.origin: The AS number that is allowed to announce the prefix.
keys.notify: Address that is told when the record changes.

status.ASSIGNED PORTABLE: APNIC: the block was given directly to an end user by APNIC or an NIR. It is provider-independent, so the holder can keep it when changing ISPs and announce it in BGP.
status.ALLOCATED PORTABLE: APNIC: a large block given to a member (LIR or NIR) to hand out to its own customers. It is provider-independent.
status.ASSIGNED NON PORTABLE: APNIC: a part of an ISP's block lent to a customer. It belongs to that ISP and goes back if the customer leaves.
status.ALLOCATED NON PORTABLE: APNIC: a part of an ISP's block set aside for further sub-allocation. It belongs to the upstream ISP.
status.ASSIGNED PA: RIPE/AFRINIC: provider-aggregatable space a member assigned to an end user. It belongs to the provider and is normally announced as part of the provider's larger block.
status.ALLOCATED PA: RIPE/AFRINIC: a block a member (LIR) received from the registry to assign to its own customers. It is announced by the member.
status.ASSIGNED PI: RIPE/AFRINIC: provider-independent space assigned to an end user. The holder keeps it when changing provider and can announce it with its own AS number.
status.SUB ALLOCATED PA: RIPE: a part of a provider's allocation handed to another ISP that assigns it onward.
status.LIR PARTITIONED PA: RIPE: a member split its allocation into smaller blocks for its own organisation.
status.ALLOCATED BY RIR: RIPE (IPv6): a large block allocated to a member by the registry.
status.ALLOCATED ASSIGNED PA: RIPE (IPv6): part of a member's allocation that is also assigned to an end user.
status.ALLOCATED UNSPECIFIED: RIPE (IPv6): a block allocated to a member without a stated purpose.
status.AGGREGATED BY LIR: RIPE (IPv6): several customer assignments are summarised under one record by the member.
status.ASSIGNED ANYCAST: RIPE: space assigned for an anycast service such as DNS or a CDN.
status.LEGACY: A block handed out before the regional registries existed (before about 1992). Holders keep it, but rules and fees can differ and the contact data is often old.
status.EARLY REGISTRATION: RIPE: a pre-RIR legacy registration kept in the database.
status.NOT SET: The holder has not set a status for this record.
status.DIRECT ALLOCATION: ARIN: a block given straight from ARIN to an ISP or large organisation.
status.DIRECT ASSIGNMENT: ARIN: a block given straight from ARIN to an end user.
status.REALLOCATED: ARIN: an ISP passed a part of its block to another ISP that can assign it further.
status.REASSIGNED: ARIN: an ISP gave a part of its block to a customer for its own use.
status.ALLOCATED: LACNIC and others: a block given to a member for further distribution.
status.ASSIGNED: LACNIC and others: a block given to an end user.
status.REALLOCATED PA: A member passed part of its allocation to another provider.
status.REASSIGNED PA: A member gave part of its allocation to an end customer.
